parsed.explanation: No visitor-facing trans-specific exposure is documented: no criminalisation of presentation, no document/screening mismatch rule, no facility, custody or care restriction, no targeting record. Structural signals are consistently positive — rule of law, a supranational rights charter applicable, a 2015 equality ordinance that expressly defines gender reassignment and gives an equality commission inquiry jurisdiction over it, and social acceptance evidenced by marriage and adoption equality. Weaknesses: the constitutional discrimination grounds omit gender reassignment (resident-facing gap, but signals incomplete protection), no documented enforcement record of the 2015 ordinance against service denial, and silence on custody/ward placement is open question rather than exposure. Dated same-sex decriminalisation is tangential. Positive, reasonably well-documented structural facts outweigh the gaps, but absent documented visitor-facing protections operating in practice it stays below the low-risk tiers.
